Root cause: double application of the host desktop offset. Android mapLocalToHost already returns absolute virtual-desktop coords (relativeX*hostW + hostLeft, RemoteDesktopScreen.kt:521), and the host DispatchInput re-added _desktopLeft/_desktopTop (RemoteDesktopHandler.cs:750/757/765), so on a non-zero-origin secondary monitor the cursor was driven off-screen and SendInput clamped it to the desktop edge (x=0). Fix: removed the host-side offset addition (Android coords are already absolute); deleted the now-dead _desktopLeft/_desktopTop fields. Primary monitor unaffected (origin 0,0). Host builds clean.

Fixed: mapLocalToHost now returns Offset? (null only on the 3 not-ready/degenerate error cases) instead of overloading Offset.Zero as both error sentinel and the valid (0,0) host origin. Verified: :app:compileDebugKotlin BUILD SUCCESSFUL. Device verification of the corner-tap still recommended.

Lone/unpaired surrogates typed best-effort as a single code unit. Added UnicodeTextInputTests (8 tests, all pass). Verified: dotnet test --filter UnicodeTextInputTests -> 8 passed. Normal BMP typing unchanged. Device verification of emoji end-to-end still recommended.

Root cause found + fixed: the modern client uses cursor-SHAPE streaming (not host compositing). DXGI TryCaptureCurrentCursorShape returned the cached _lastPointerShape without refreshing; that cache is only updated by the main frame loop, which doesn't run on a static screen — so a cursor-shape change over an unchanging screen (arrow->hand over a link) was missed (~5%). The 10Hz cursor sync now forces a DXGI pointer-shape refresh (reusing the existing null-triggered refresh path, guarded by _lock.Wait(0) so it never races the main loop's AcquireNextFrame). Host builds; tests green (244/244). Requires host redeploy + on-device recheck to confirm the residual ~5% is gone.

Root cause: DxgiDesktopCapture re-created the DXGI duplication (DuplicateOutput) on every DXGI_ERROR_ACCESS_LOST, throttling only on re-init exceptions. Since access-loss returns the cached frame, the stream loop saw 'success' and never backed off, so DuplicateOutput ran at full frame rate (up to 120Hz) against a display mid power-transition (idle monitor-off), wedging DWM (dwmredir.dll) + the NVIDIA driver -> host black-screen-with-cursor, CAD/Win+Ctrl+Shift+B unrecoverable. Fix: new DuplicationReinitThrottle rate-limits re-init (1 attempt per escalating 1s->8s window, reset by any healthy frame) wired into TryReinitializeDuplication + TryRecover; healthy-frame reset added to both capture paths + cursor-shape refresh. 8 unit tests pass; no regressions (the 11 other failures are pre-existing, tracked separately). CHANGELOG updated. Defense-in-depth display-power gating filed as follow-up.

CHANGELOG updated. Files: FakeScreenCaptureService.cs (new), RemexHostFactory.cs, ScreenCaptureFakeRegistrationTests.cs (new). Production root-cause (eager DXGI init at startup) tracked separately as RemEx-hmj.
